newsitem.title: FRANCE: France seeks to limit Thursday flights due strike.
newsitem.headline: France seeks to limit Thursday flights due strike.

text.p: France's civil aviation authority has asked airlines to limit flights to and from France on Thursday as air traffic controllers will provide only a minimum service due to a one-day strike, a spokesman said on Monday.
The spokesman for the Direction Generale de l'Aviation Civile (DGAC) told Reuters that French law stipulated that a minimum service meant maintaining "50 percent capacity for air traffic control".
The DGAC has received strike notices from three unions for Thursday's national stoppage by public sector workers and civil servants protesting against the government's austerity budget for 1997.
Reduced air traffic control may affect overflights over France which account for about half the traffic handled by French controllers.

Between 2,500 and 3,000 planes take off and land at French airports daily. The DGAC has asked airlines to restrict flights to the most important destinations and services, such as express deliveries, the spokesman said.
